title: Home Sweet Home
intro: In Linux, commands often accept options (also called flags) that modify how a program behaves. They are typed after the command name and usually start with a single dash for short names (like -v) or a double dash for full words (like --version). Most command-line programs include a built-in option that prints out usage instructions and lists every flag the program supports.
story: /challenge/run can give you the flag, but only if you ask nicely and do what it tells you to do.
description:
Check /challenge/run's documentation to find the option for asking nicely.
Run the program with that option and follow the instructions it gives you.
